newsitem.title: USA: MEAT - Poultry seen gaining in U.S. over beef, pork.
newsitem.headline: MEAT - Poultry seen gaining in U.S. over beef, pork.

text.p: Poultry will likely gain some market share in the United States at the expense of beef and pork, panelists at a conference said Friday.
The gain over beef will be slightly greater than over pork, as recent trends of high cattle inventories and lower prices begin to reverse themselves, the panelists said.

Pork's market share will hold up better than beef because of integration, genetic improvements and other pork industry efficiencies, the participants in a roundtable discussion at the National Broiler Council's annual meeting said.
Analyst Jeff Walser of the Philadelphia-based WEFA group Thursday predicted a 5.6 percent rise this year in U.S. broiler production, which he said would reach 26.4 billion pounds.
With lower feed prices, similar growth could be expected in 1997, Walser said.
Meanwhile, Slamecka warned against too-rapid expansion of exports.
"We should look at exports as a business just like any other, and not just as a place to put something," he said. "Unbridled growth ... in production capacity wbe a detriment to all of us."
Monty Henderson, President and Chief Operating Officer of George's Inc, a Springdale, Arkansas, poultry producer, said that per-capita meat consumption in the United States had likely reached a peak.
Changes in market share between each meat group would now be driven almost entirely by price, he said.
"I think it's a matter of relative price. We've reached saturation on the amount of meat we can eat," Henderson said.
Panel members also said they were skeptical that export markets would continue to sustain domestic production to the extent estimated by analysts at the conference Thursday.
